# pyvectorfit

> Python library for vector fitting of delayed pole-residue models for electromagnetic transient
> (EMT) simulation: rational fitting, universal line models with searched modal delays, and
> passivity assessment and enforcement, on plain NumPy arrays.

Install with `pip install pyvectorfit`, for Python 3.11 to 3.14. Frequencies are in Hz; poles,
residues and `s` in rad/s; delays in s. Samples have shape `(len(f), *shape)`, and every fit
returns `model, report`. A model is its poles, residues and delays, saved with `to_dict()`.
pyvectorfit takes per-metre `z` (Ω/m) and `y` (S/m) and does not compute them.

## Docs

- [Start here](https://pyvectorfit.readthedocs.io/en/latest/): installation and a line model quickstart
- [Guide](https://pyvectorfit.readthedocs.io/en/latest/guide.html): conventions, the model, and the methods behind each step
- [API](https://pyvectorfit.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html): fit, fit_line, check_passivity, enforce_passivity, recursive_convolution and their reports
- [Examples](https://pyvectorfit.readthedocs.io/en/latest/gallery/index.html): fitting Yc, line models, modal delays, passivity, transients

## Optional

- [Benchmarks](https://pyvectorfit.readthedocs.io/en/latest/benchmarks.html): accuracy on six overhead lines and cables
- [Source](https://github.com/BirchfieldResearchGroup/pyvectorfit/tree/main/src/pyvectorfit): the package and its docstrings
- [OpenLine](https://openline.readthedocs.io/llms.txt): line constants of overhead lines, from conductor and structure catalogs
